title: Program Kit deterministic host-tooling extensions
intent: Extend the implemented Program Kit with provider-neutral operation convergence, typed .NET configuration and Options generation, structured diagnostics and observability, deterministic ASP.NET Core transport-failure handling, standards-profiled confidential and public OIDC clients, JWT resource servers, OAuth service clients and token exchange, external OpenAPI client generation, Aspire and Dev Container projections, and bounded optional adapters without importing consumer-domain meaning.
scope: A compact Orbyss.ProgramKit.Operations contract package that becomes the one canonical source for operation identity and host projections.

Explicit ordered .NET configuration-source composition, typed Options binding, startup validation, provider reload capabilities, and consumer-selected IOptions, IOptionsSnapshot, or IOptionsMonitor semantics.
Built-in .NET configuration provider profiles plus an explicitly registered custom-provider generation ABI.

Structured .NET logging, tracing, metrics, correlation, transport telemetry, exception observation, and controlled provider/exporter composition through platform emission APIs and a pinned OpenTelemetry adapter.
Deterministic ASP.NET Core transport-failure handling through Problem Details, ordered exception handlers, explicit middleware and diagnostics behavior, and consumer-owned error mapping.
Optional Azure Key Vault and Azure App Configuration provider adapters with external credentials, bounded refresh, and secret-safe evidence.
ASP.NET Core authentication and authorization host profiles for confidential interactive OpenID Connect clients and OAuth JWT resource servers.

A public browser OIDC authorization-code-with-PKCE profile, an initial pinned Blazor WebAssembly projection, automated local browser conformance, and optional operator-assisted real-provider acceptance.
Explicit OAuth client-credentials and RFC 8693 token-exchange profiles for service clients without inferred delegation, scope, audience, or consumer-domain authorization.
Deterministic external OpenAPI client generation through an exact pinned Kiota adapter.
Deterministic Aspire AppHost source generation from explicit application composition input.
Deterministic Dev Container artifact generation and validation from explicit development-container input.
An optional FastEndpoints projection of the same owned operation contracts.
An Aspire-backed, ephemeral Keycloak local-test fixture proving provider substitution and realm import without production provisioning.
nonGoals: No consumer-domain Identity, Authorization, role, grant, policy, principal, entitlement, environment, workspace, deployment, or release semantics.
No claim that OAuth 2.0 authenticates an end user or that an ID token is an API access token.
No assumption that every OAuth access token is a JWT; opaque-token introspection remains a deferred profile.
No provider-neutral reinterpretation of provider-specific claims, groups, roles, scopes, or tenant conventions.
No provider discovery, issuer selection, dynamic client registration, network retrieval, secret retrieval, or token acquisition during deterministic generation.
No custom general-purpose OpenAPI client generator.
No comprehensive direct Docker Compose model or Program Kit-owned container orchestrator.
No automatic Aspire, Docker Compose, container, Dev Container, Keycloak, Azure, deployment, or infrastructure execution.
No production Keycloak provisioning, backup, migration, or administration.
No generated arbitrary configuration-provider behavior from an unconstrained type name or script.
No guarantee that a changed configuration value can recompose middleware, dependency injection, listeners, serialization profiles, database providers, or other restart-required host topology.
No silent last-known-good guarantee beyond the exact .NET Options behavior selected and proven by fixtures; a stronger runtime controller requires a separate approved design.

No application or consumer-domain observability meaning, business event catalog, security audit ledger, compliance record, incident policy, alert rule, dashboard, retention policy, telemetry backend, collector, or storage service.

No request or response body, authorization header, token, cookie, claim payload, configuration value, secret, personal value, raw exception payload, or unbounded metric attribute is captured by default.
No assumption that every OpenTelemetry semantic-convention group is stable or that an SDK's current default convention is a durable Program Kit contract.
No automatic telemetry emission from Program Kit generation, validation, design, or development-session tools.
No inference from an exception type or message to consumer-domain error meaning or an HTTP status; every non-generic mapping is explicit and consumer-owned.
No claim that browser automation proves protocol security or that real-provider acceptance is deterministic canonical generation evidence.
No device authorization, CIBA, FAPI, DPoP, implicit, resource-owner-password, or dynamic client-registration profile in the initial capability set.
assumptions: The approved Program Kit baseline at version 0.3.0 remains authoritative except where this extension is later approved as an explicit compatible or breaking revision.
The extension continues to target the repository-pinned .NET 10 and C# 14 profile and preserves exact package, source, license, and transitive-closure verification.
OAuth 2.0 protocol behavior is governed by applicable IETF standards and current security best current practice; OpenID Connect behavior is governed by approved OpenID Foundation specifications.

The initial interactive profiles distinguish a preferred confidential server-side/BFF client from an explicitly selected public browser client; both use authorization code flow with PKCE, while the public client has no client secret and is not represented as the preferred architecture for sensitive applications.

The initial public browser target is a pinned Blazor WebAssembly OIDC projection behind a versioned browser-target adapter boundary; additional browser targets require separately selected adapters rather than generic JavaScript generation.
A public-client refresh token is absent or rotated in the initial profile while DPoP and other sender-constrained-token profiles remain deferred.

OAuth client credentials and RFC 8693 token exchange are separate, optional initial profiles with exact client authentication, subject/actor token, delegation/impersonation, resource, audience, scope, requested-token and issued-token declarations.

The initial API profile accepts only JWT access tokens satisfying the selected issuer, audience, signature algorithm, lifetime, metadata, and token-profile requirements; it never accepts an ID token as an access token.

ASP.NET Core middleware constructs an AuthenticationTicket and ClaimsPrincipal as transport-host results. A consumer adapter must explicitly translate any required material into consumer-domain Identity or Authorization inputs.

A standards-conforming provider product is substitutable only when its exact metadata, algorithms, endpoints, client registration, token profile, and claim mappings satisfy the selected Program Kit host profile.
Configuration sources are ordered explicitly because later .NET configuration providers override earlier providers for the same key.
Reload is available only when a selected provider emits a change token or an explicit bounded refresh mechanism triggers one.

IOptionsSnapshot is scoped and provides one consistent value per scope; IOptionsMonitor is singleton-capable and provides current values and change notification. Neither can safely recompose arbitrary host topology.
Required and security-critical options validate on start. Live reload is opt-in per binding and fails closed when the provider cannot satisfy the declared reload capability.
Source-generated configuration binding and Options validation are preferred where the owned options type and selected .NET profile support them.
.NET libraries emit provider-neutral diagnostics through ILogger, ActivitySource, and Meter; generated application hosts own collection, filtering, sampling, processing, and export selection.
OpenTelemetry is an optional provider adapter over .NET platform emission APIs and never becomes the semantic owner of Program Kit operation or transport observations.
The OpenTelemetry specification, semantic-convention revision, .NET SDK packages, instrumentation packages, exporters, and stability opt-ins are exact independent selections.
W3C Trace Context is the initial distributed-correlation profile; baggage is untrusted transport metadata and cannot establish identity, authorization, or unrestricted telemetry attributes.

Framework and selected OpenTelemetry instrumentation are preferred for ASP.NET Core and HttpClient; custom middleware adds only missing Program Kit-owned correlation and bounded operation attributes and must not duplicate spans or logs.

ASP.NET Core exception observation and response handling are separate concerns. The selected transport-failure profile explicitly composes Problem Details, ordered IExceptionHandler registrations, middleware order, status-code pages, response-started behavior, cancellation classification, content negotiation, and .NET 10 handled-exception diagnostic suppression.

Public-browser verification is layered: protocol tests are deterministic; Playwright for .NET drives isolated local browsers and Aspire-backed fixtures; real-provider interaction is opt-in and may pause for a human without capturing credentials; threat-model acceptance remains a human decision.

Logging filters may support controlled configuration reload, but the OpenTelemetry provider, processor, instrumentation, and exporter graph is startup-fixed unless a selected revision explicitly proves safe reconfiguration.
External OpenAPI documents are foreign contract inputs; Program Kit-owned OpenAPI remains a projection of owned operation contracts and never becomes a competing source of behavior.
Aspire AppHost, Dev Container, FastEndpoints, Keycloak realm, and Kiota outputs are provider projections bound to exact canonical inputs and tool/provider versions.

sourceTruthAuthorities.governs: The human-started scope, aligned ordering, explicit deferrals, protocol distinctions, and design authority boundary.
The implemented Program Kit ownership, dependency, generation, determinism, package, capability, and non-domain baseline.

The accepted-intake separation between transport authentication and Engine Identity/Authorization, the prospective Operations convergence requirement, and the Dev Container versus governed-work boundaries; it grants no Engine implementation authority.

domains.purpose: Own reusable, deterministic software construction and host-integration mechanics without importing consumer-domain meaning.

vocabulary.meaning: An exact standards-backed selection of roles, flows, metadata, validation requirements, security constraints, and supported variations that a host and provider binding must satisfy.
A technology-specific adapter that satisfies an explicit base contract or protocol profile without replacing its semantic owner.
An explicit ordered selection of IConfigurationSource behavior whose precedence, startup, reload, secret, and failure characteristics are reviewed.
A typed relationship between one owned options type, configuration section, optional name, validation rules, startup requirement, and permitted reload consumption.
A provider-declared and fixture-proven ability to publish a configuration change token after obtaining a newer effective value under explicit timing and failure rules.
A structured log, trace activity, metric measurement, or bounded event emitted for observation without becoming an authoritative business, security, audit, or compliance record.
An explicit host selection of diagnostic sources, instrumentation, resource attributes, filters, sampling, processors, exporters, redaction, cardinality, shutdown, and failure behavior.

An explicit ASP.NET Core selection of exception handlers, Problem Details serialization, middleware order, status-code handling, diagnostic disposition, and consumer-owned mappings from transport-relevant failures to HTTP responses.

An opt-in headed-browser verification mode in which a human completes provider-controlled interaction and automation resumes only to verify declared application outcomes without capturing credentials or granting approval.
Generated source or configuration derived from canonical operation, composition, configuration, and provider selections; it is not a second semantic owner.
An externally owned artifact such as an OpenAPI document whose exact bytes and provenance are inputs to an integration generator.

semanticModels.meaning: The ordered host configuration source selections and their provider, precedence, startup, reload, secret, failure, package, and compatibility declarations.
semanticModels.invariants: Order is explicit and stable; duplicate or conflicting provider identities fail; every provider is exact-version selected; reload is declared rather than inferred; secret values never enter canonical intent, generated evidence, or diagnostics.

semanticModels.meaning: The typed binding from an owned .NET options type to one section and optional name with exact validation, startup, and reload disposition.
semanticModels.invariants: Required bindings validate on start; named options are explicit; IOptionsSnapshot is never injected into singleton-generated infrastructure; live monitoring requires provider reload support; restart-required options cannot select live monitoring.

semanticModels.meaning: The selected .NET logging, tracing, metrics, correlation, instrumentation, sampling, processing, exporter, redaction, cardinality, failure, and shutdown mechanics for one generated host.
semanticModels.invariants: Libraries emit only through reviewed platform APIs; host collection and export are explicit; source and instrument names are stable and versioned; semantic-convention revisions and stability opt-ins are exact; metric dimensions are bounded; sensitive values are excluded by default; diagnostic signals never grant authority or become durable audit truth; telemetry failure does not silently change application outcomes.

semanticModels.meaning: The ASP.NET Core mechanics that deterministically convert explicitly classified transport failures into safe negotiated HTTP responses while coordinating exception diagnostics.
semanticModels.invariants: Problem Details and handler order are explicit; generic unhandled failures disclose no internal detail; cancellation and response-started cases are distinct; handled-exception diagnostic suppression is selected explicitly; no exception name or message invents consumer-domain meaning.

semanticModels.meaning: The standards and ASP.NET Core mechanics required for one exact host authentication role and its authorization-policy attachment points.
semanticModels.invariants: OAuth is not reported as authentication; confidential clients, public browser clients, service clients and resource servers remain distinct; ID tokens are not API access tokens; public clients carry no secret; token exchange distinguishes impersonation from delegation; issuer, audience, resource, scope, token types, algorithms, metadata and HTTPS rules are explicit; provider claims do not become consumer-domain conclusions.

semanticModels.meaning: The binding from canonical or foreign inputs and exact tool/provider selections to every generated output and its digest.
semanticModels.invariants: Generation never uses ambient discovery; identical inputs and exact tool versions produce byte-identical normalized outputs; foreign inputs remain foreign-owned; generated outputs carry source and tool provenance.

referenceRules.referencedScope: Its declared Program Kit base contract package and exact external technology packages only
referenceRules.rationale: Technology dependencies and quirks remain isolated from provider-neutral contracts.

referenceRules.referencedScope: Orbyss.ProgramKit.Workbench, Orbyss.ProgramKit.DotNet generation assemblies, CommandLine, agent capabilities, or design-time provider adapters at runtime
referenceRules.rationale: Generated consumers carry only selected runtime dependencies and generated source, not the tools that produced them.

referenceRules.referencingScope: Program Kit protocol, ASP.NET Core failure/security, public-browser, OAuth service-client, Keycloak, Entra, configuration, and host-generation components
referenceRules.referencedScope: Consumer-domain Identity, Authorization, role, grant, policy, principal, entitlement, admission, or evidence semantics

referenceRules.referencingScope: Program Kit diagnostics, logging, tracing, metrics, transport instrumentation, OpenTelemetry, exporter, and host-generation components

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent the agreed Program Kit host-tooling extension scope and architectural boundaries as a validated canonical design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design carries architecture meaning and grants no runtime or implementation behavior.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The design is schema-validated, reviewed against its exact sources, digest-bound by its plan, and compared during implementation closure.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The repository artifact is explicit input and not discovered through an agent retrieval system.

agentProcedure.rationale: The design does not define, register, or authorize an agent capability.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit architecture reviewer and implementers.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only an explicit human decision over the exact design and plan digests may approve implementation.
humanCommunication.rationale: A human-readable Markdown projection and review manifest make exact scope and tradeoffs reviewable.

generatedNavigation.rationale: No separate generated navigation artifact is required for this bounded review set.

governance.provenancePolicy: The exact human intent record, approved Program Kit baseline, accepted Engine intake boundary, source commit, and consulted external standards are named; no later implementation is treated as retroactive design authority.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest and plan bind exact canonical design bytes; changes require regenerated projection, validation, digest, and renewed human decision.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Any ownership, authority, dependency, protocol, wire, generation, reload, or provider-boundary change requires explicit compatibility review and a new design version.
governance.migrationPolicy: Implementation must migrate DotNetOperationBinding, shell/configuration contracts, package/version maps, fixtures, and generated hosts through bounded work units with no parallel semantic owner.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: No credentials, tokens, secrets, personal claims, tenant values, or provider payloads are included.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: The repository review set and its human-readable Markdown projection are the only intended externalizations.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Runtime provider observations, discovered metadata, generated secrets, tokens, caches, tool output, and local container state remain outside the canonical design.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A schema-governed design instance is the canonical authority for the extension while implementation remains blocked pending exact human approval.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Provide a stable human-readable review projection of the canonical host-tooling design.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The review projection is compared with the canonical design and digest-bound in the review manifest.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The projection is an explicit repository file.

agentProcedure.rationale: The projection contains no capability procedure.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit architecture reviewer and implementers.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: The projection explains the design but only explicit approval of the canonical design and plan digests grants implementation authority.
humanCommunication.rationale: Markdown is the deliberate reviewer-oriented representation.

generatedNavigation.generationRule: Maintain stable reviewer-oriented sections from the exact canonical design and consulted authorities.
generatedNavigation.rationale: Stable sections make the canonical design reviewable.

representation.projectionRule: Project the outcome, scope, boundaries, ordering, evidence, and consulted sources from the canonical architecture design.
representation.lossPolicy: The projection is intentionally lossy; canonical JSON remains authoritative for exact machine fields.

governance.provenancePolicy: The exact canonical design and named external authorities are the only content inputs.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest binds the exact Markdown bytes and the canonical design digest.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Update and re-review whenever the canonical design changes.
governance.migrationPolicy: Reproject from the canonical design rather than treating Markdown as a competing architecture owner.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: No sensitive values are accepted from the canonical design or consulted sources.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: The committed Markdown file is the intended human-readable externalization.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: No runtime provider observation, discovered metadata, token, secret, or local state is included.

artifactDecisions.rationale: The Markdown document is a review projection of the canonical JSON design.

representationRelationships.projectionRule: Project stable reviewer-oriented Markdown sections from the canonical architecture design and named consulted authorities.
representationRelationships.lossPolicy: The canonical JSON retains exact machine fields and remains authoritative when the Markdown projection omits detail.

security.policy: Program Kit validates and projects exact transport-security profiles; providers perform protocol behavior; consumers own domain identity and authorization.
guarantees: Interactive ID-token validation and API access-token validation remain distinct.
Confidential, public-browser, service-client and resource-server roles remain distinct; a public client never carries a client secret.

Issuer, audience, resource, scope, HTTPS metadata, algorithms, token kind, lifetime, client type, redirect URI, PKCE, refresh disposition, subject token, actor token, delegation or impersonation, and claim mapping are explicit and fail closed.
Secrets and tokens never enter generated source, canonical intent, logs, or evidence.
exclusions: No user authentication server, credential store, token issuer, role model, domain authorization engine, or security authority is created.
No provider product is trusted merely because it exposes an OIDC-looking endpoint.
No token is ambiently forwarded or exchanged, and no requested scope, audience, resource, delegation or impersonation authority is inferred.

authority.policy: Only humans approve designs, plans, provider selections, credentials, execution, and consumer policy; generated artifacts and protocol outcomes grant no authority.
guarantees: Anonymous versus authenticated transport disposition and named ASP.NET Core policy attachment are explicit.
A ClaimsPrincipal and token claims are observations available to consumer adapters, not permission conclusions.
exclusions: No inferred role, scope, claim, group, tenant, or provider mapping grants a consumer-domain operation.

secrets.policy: Canonical inputs carry secret references and credential-selection policy only; providers resolve values at runtime.
guarantees: Generated source, configuration templates, locks, manifests, diagnostics, tests, and receipts are secret-free.
Azure, confidential OIDC, client-credentials and token-exchange adapters prefer managed identity, certificates, assertions, or externally supplied credential abstractions where supported.
Playwright authentication state, browser traces, cookies and tokens are ephemeral secret material, excluded from source control and redacted or destroyed under the selected test profile.
exclusions: No client secret, private key, access token, refresh token, password, vault secret value, or generated Keycloak credential is persisted as Program Kit evidence.

persistence.policy: Only canonical design inputs, normalized generated artifacts, locks, provenance, and redacted evidence are durable.
guarantees: Provider caches, discovery metadata, tokens, local container volumes, generated credentials, and runtime Options values remain ephemeral or provider-owned.
Keycloak fixture state is disposable and never treated as backup or migration material.
exclusions: No Program Kit identity store, authorization store, deployment state, configuration control plane, or secret store is introduced.

failure.policy: Unknown provider capability, invalid configuration, invalid token profile, stale or conflicting input, missing package evidence, and nondeterministic output fail closed with stable diagnostics.
guarantees: Required Options validate before host readiness.
Reload-provider outages, invalid reload candidates, metadata/key rollover failures, Kiota errors, and generator drift are distinguishable.
No failed reload is reported as successful reconfiguration.
Unhandled transport failures receive a safe generic response unless the response has started; explicit mappings, cancellation and client disconnects remain distinguishable.
Handled-exception diagnostic emission is an explicit .NET profile choice so one failure is not accidentally logged or counted twice.
exclusions: No universal retry, fallback identity provider, silent default audience, permissive algorithm, insecure metadata, stale-value guarantee, or exception-name-to-status convention is invented.

concurrency.policy: Generation is isolated per explicit output root; live configuration changes have declared ordering and consumer-owned application semantics.
guarantees: Identical generation invocations do not race through shared mutable caches or output directories.
IOptionsSnapshot provides scope consistency and IOptionsMonitor subscriptions are disposable.
Async reconfiguration is queued by consumer-owned bounded services rather than executed unbounded inside change callbacks.
exclusions: No atomic distributed reconfiguration, cross-process configuration transaction, or automatic service reconstruction is claimed.

cancellation.policy: Bounded generation and external-tool operations accept cancellation and report whether outputs are absent, partial, or complete.
guarantees: Cancellation stops further generation and never promotes partial output as valid.
Local fixture teardown is attempted within its declared ownership boundary.
exclusions: Cancellation does not roll back provider-side effects, remote token activity, or external state not owned by the operation.

observability.policy: Generated hosts expose stable structured logs, traces, metrics, W3C correlation, provider/profile identity, reload outcome, and redacted evidence through exact platform and provider selections without making telemetry authoritative.
guarantees: Evidence records identities, versions, digests, timings or sequence where relevant, and success/failure classification without values classified as secret.
ILogger categories and event IDs, ActivitySource names and versions, Meter names, instruments, units, and bounded attributes are stable reviewed contracts.
OpenTelemetry specification, semantic-convention, SDK, instrumentation, exporter, and stability opt-in revisions are selected independently and exactly.
Framework instrumentation is preferred for ASP.NET Core and HttpClient, and fixtures reject duplicate transport spans or logs.
Sampling, filtering, batching, exporter outage, bounded flush, telemetry drop, sensitive-data exclusion, and metric-cardinality behavior are explicit.

Fixtures observe provider substitution, reload notification, scoped consistency, token rejection and exchange, browser redirects and storage, transport-failure handling, cross-transport correlation, telemetry redaction, and generated-output determinism.
exclusions: No token, authorization material, cookie, claim payload, configuration value, secret name-value pair, personal data, request or response body, raw exception payload, raw provider response, or unbounded attribute is recorded by default.
No diagnostic signal is a business event ledger, security audit record, compliance record, authorization decision, or guaranteed delivery channel.
No telemetry backend, collector, dashboard, alert, retention rule, or incident policy is owned by Program Kit.

compatibility.policy: Protocol standards, .NET behavior, external tools, provider packages, generated wire/source surfaces, and Program Kit contracts version independently and are joined by exact selections.
guarantees: Every external version and package digest is locked and source/license reviewed before implementation selection.
Existing DotNet shell and operation bindings migrate through explicit Version Map and impact assessment.
Provider-specific changes cannot silently alter the base profile.
exclusions: No floating latest package, image, feature, SDK, specification draft, discovery result, or provider default is treated as durable compatibility evidence.

scenarios.intent: Emit safe correlated logs, traces, and metrics for inbound transport, owned operation dispatch, outbound HTTP, and failures through an exact host-selected OpenTelemetry composition.
preconditions: Signal sources, instruments, resource identity, W3C propagation, filters, sampling, processors, exporter, redaction, cardinality, exception, shutdown, package, specification and semantic-convention revisions are explicit.
steps: Generate stable ILogger categories and source-generated event methods, ActivitySource and Meter declarations, and host resource identity.
Register framework ASP.NET Core and HttpClient instrumentation once and add only missing bounded Program Kit operation observations.
Compose exact sampling, processing and exporter behavior after typed startup validation.
Exercise inbound-to-operation-to-outbound correlation, expected and unexpected failures, sampling, exporter outage, shutdown, redaction, bounded cardinality and duplicate-signal rejection.
outcomes: Selected signals correlate through W3C trace context without becoming identity or authorization evidence.
Telemetry provider failure remains distinguishable and does not silently alter successful application behavior.
A different conforming exporter can replace OTLP without changing Program Kit signal ownership.
failureOutcomes: Unstable or unpinned convention, duplicate instrumentation, sensitive field, unbounded attribute, invalid exporter configuration, blocking critical-path export, or unbounded shutdown fails validation or the fixture.

scenarios.intent: Bind owned typed Options against an explicit provider composition with startup validation and declared reload consumption.
preconditions: The options type, section, schema, validator, provider selections, order, packages, and reload disposition are exact inputs.
steps: Validate provider capabilities and deterministic precedence.
Generate provider registration and OptionsBuilder binding with startup validation.
Build the isolated generated host.
Exercise startup-fixed, scoped snapshot, and live monitor fixtures against supported providers.
Reject invalid startup, invalid reload, incompatible lifetime, secret leakage, and unsupported reload.
outcomes: Required configuration fails before readiness when invalid.
Scoped consumers observe one consistent snapshot per scope.
Monitor consumers observe only provider-signaled and successfully rebound values under the declared semantics.
failureOutcomes: A provider outage, malformed value, conflicting source, or unsupported reload produces a stable redacted diagnostic and no false success.

scenarios.intent: Turn an explicitly classified transport failure into a safe negotiated HTTP response without inventing consumer-domain error meaning or duplicating diagnostics.
preconditions: The Problem Details profile, handler order, middleware order, environment disclosure policy, status-code-page disposition, content negotiation, cancellation classification, response-started behavior, explicit consumer mappings and diagnostic suppression choice are exact.
steps: Generate AddProblemDetails, ordered IExceptionHandler registration and UseExceptionHandler in the selected pipeline position.
Apply an explicit consumer-owned transport mapping when one matches, otherwise use the safe generic fallback.
Coordinate handled-exception logging, tracing and metrics under the pinned .NET behavior.
Exercise handled, unhandled, invalid-mapping, cancellation, response-started, development and production response cases.
outcomes: The client receives only the selected safe transport representation.
The same failure produces the declared diagnostic outcome exactly once.
FastEndpoints and Minimal API projections preserve the same failure contract.
failureOutcomes: Raw exception detail, secret leakage, inferred domain mapping, duplicate diagnostics, middleware-order drift, invalid content negotiation, or a false response rewrite after headers start fails validation or the fixture.

scenarios.intent: Authenticate an interactive user through any provider satisfying the exact OIDC profile without provider-specific application semantics.
preconditions: Issuer, client registration reference, redirect URIs, cookie profile, scopes, claim mapping, metadata and algorithm requirements are explicit.
The provider metadata satisfies the selected OIDC profile.
steps: Generate ASP.NET Core cookie and OpenID Connect scheme registration in the required middleware order.
Use authorization code flow with PKCE and exact redirect handling.
Validate metadata, issuer, nonce, state, ID-token signature, audience, lifetime, and selected claims.
Construct the transport ClaimsPrincipal and expose only the declared mapped observation to a consumer adapter.
outcomes: Keycloak, Entra ID, or another conforming provider can satisfy the same host profile through configuration and optional provider specialization.
Provider substitution does not change consumer-domain Identity or Authorization ownership.
failureOutcomes: Issuer, metadata, algorithm, redirect, state, nonce, token, or mapping mismatch fails authentication without fallback.

scenarios.intent: Authenticate through an exact OIDC public-client profile and call a protected API without a client secret or inferred application authorization.
preconditions: Authority, public client identifier, exact redirect and post-logout URIs, browser origins, scopes, PKCE, state, nonce, token storage, refresh rotation or absence, API resource and threat acceptance are explicit.
steps: Generate the pinned Blazor WebAssembly OIDC adapter and no client secret.
Run deterministic protocol vectors for redirects, PKCE, state, nonce, issuer, token kind, refresh and origin behavior.
Use Playwright for .NET against an explicitly started isolated Aspire/provider fixture to exercise login, callback, protected API access, refresh where selected, logout and negative paths.

When a real provider requires human-controlled interaction, open a headed browser, pause without capturing credentials, resume after callback and record only redacted non-authoritative acceptance evidence.
outcomes: The public client completes authorization code flow with PKCE and the API accepts only the intended access token.
Automated local evidence remains deterministic and operator-assisted provider evidence remains explicitly separate.
A confidential server-side/BFF profile remains the preferred default for sensitive applications.
failureOutcomes: Client secret generation, implicit flow, password flow, redirect or origin mismatch, state or nonce failure, token in URL/log/source, unsafe refresh persistence, hidden human authority, trace leakage, or browser/provider drift fails the applicable fixture.

scenarios.intent: Acquire a client-credentials token or perform RFC 8693 token exchange through an exact optional profile without ambient token forwarding or invented delegation.
preconditions: The selected grant/profile, token endpoint, client authentication reference, resource, audience, scope, requested token type, subject token type and provenance, optional actor token and delegation-versus-impersonation intent are explicit.
steps: Validate provider metadata and selected profile support.
Resolve client authentication only through the declared runtime secret, certificate, assertion or managed-identity-compatible reference.
Construct the exact client-credentials or token-exchange request and validate the response token type and lifetime.
Cache only under explicit subject, actor, resource, audience, scope and expiry keys; redact all token material from evidence.
outcomes: A service obtains only the explicitly requested transport token under the declared client role.
Token exchange preserves the distinction between delegation and impersonation without creating consumer-domain permission.
failureOutcomes: Missing client authentication, wrong token type, invalid issuer or audience, actor confusion, replay, overbroad scope, unsupported exchange, provider outage, token leakage, or cache-key collision fails closed.

scenarios.intent: Validate a JWT access token and attach an exact named transport authorization policy without accepting an ID token or inventing domain permission.
preconditions: Expected issuer, audience, token profile, algorithms, metadata source, clock policy, authentication scheme, operation and policy references are explicit.
steps: Generate JWT bearer registration and authentication before authorization middleware.
Validate signature, issuer, audience, token kind, lifetime and exact profile requirements.
Map the authenticated transport principal to the operation adapter.
Invoke the named ASP.NET Core policy supplied by the consumer composition.
outcomes: A valid access token yields an authenticated transport principal.
Authorization remains a separate explicit evaluation and consumer-domain decisions remain outside Program Kit.
failureOutcomes: An ID token, opaque token, wrong issuer or audience, forbidden algorithm, expired token, invalid signature, missing policy, or denied policy fails closed.

scenarios.intent: Generate a strongly typed client from one exact local external OpenAPI document using a pinned Kiota toolchain.
preconditions: The OpenAPI bytes, language, namespace, class name, include/exclude selections, serializers, output root, Kiota version and package policy are explicit.
steps: Validate and digest the foreign OpenAPI input in an allow-listed foreign-document boundary.
Run the exact pinned Kiota adapter with isolated cache and output.
Normalize allowed outputs and record the Kiota lock and generated-tree digest.
Build an isolated package-only consumer and verify authentication injection contains no secret.
outcomes: Identical inputs and tool versions produce byte-identical normalized source and provenance.
External contract ownership remains explicit.
failureOutcomes: Unsupported OpenAPI, tool drift, network dependency, nondeterministic output, package conflict, or compilation error fails generation.

scenarios.intent: Generate a deterministic .devcontainer directory from exact development-container inputs without executing lifecycle behavior.
preconditions: Image or Dockerfile/Compose references, features, mounts, ports, user, editor metadata and scripts are explicit.
steps: Validate the selected Dev Container specification profile and pinned feature references.
Treat lifecycle scripts as opaque files bound by path and digest.
Generate canonical JSON-compatible devcontainer metadata and referenced artifacts.
Validate paths, secrets, forbidden privilege defaults and repeatability.

No production-hardening or governed-work claim is made.

scenarios.intent: Prove the same OIDC and JWT host profiles with an ephemeral Keycloak instance orchestrated by a generated Aspire AppHost.
preconditions: Keycloak image, Aspire integration, realm import subset, clients, redirect URIs, token profile, claims and ephemeral storage are exact fixture inputs.
steps: Generate the AppHost and realm import without users, passwords or client-secret values in source.
Start an isolated instance only through an explicit test profile.
Exercise discovery, interactive authentication, API token validation, key rollover and declared claim mapping.
Destroy fixture-owned resources and retain only redacted evidence.
outcomes: Keycloak proves one optional provider specialization while the generated application profiles remain provider-neutral.
failureOutcomes: Persistent state, import skip ambiguity, version drift, secret capture, provider-specific semantic leakage, teardown failure or protocol mismatch fails the fixture.
